reports.title: Choose worthwhile campaigns—and measure the right traffic
reports.intro: Today’s research focuses on campaign fit and production economics. A later follow-up adds a measurement check and newly announced maintenance. These practices are not promises of earnings.
reports.scope: Amazon.com US is the working assumption. Recommendations about Affiliate+ and Sponsored Products for Creators apply only if Casey is eligible. Offsite Associates links and onsite Influencer content are separate contexts.
reports.coverage: Morning public research was supplemented later on October 6 by a read-only review of about nine newest posts and visible administrator replies in the approved private group, after verifying the Chrome profile and Facebook identity. Only public-source-supported findings appear in this portable brief. Public URL Vue documentation and the live Viral Vue status page were also checked. Primary Amazon guide passages were available through the search index; direct full-PDF retrieval remained incomplete. No campaign, account or social action was taken.

findings.title: Check the campaign before spending time on new assets
findings.body: Amazon describes a campaign bonus for qualifying purchases of covered products, from the sponsoring seller, during an active funded campaign. A familiar title or attractive rate alone is not enough.
findings.action: For five products already in Casey’s gallery, record the exact ASIN/variation, sponsoring seller, eligibility and acceptance status, start/end dates, budget status, audience fit and realistic production time. Shortlist only products that still make sense to recommend. This is a human review; nothing has been accepted or changed.
findings.measure: Record review time and how many proposed assets are redirected before production. Once a human approves a campaign, compare actual net commissions with the time spent making and maintaining its content.
findings.evidence: Primary Amazon guide and Amazon Ads help, retrieved as indexed excerpts. Workflow and prioritization are analyst proposals; Casey’s eligibility, campaigns and results were not inspected.
findings.source_date: Undated Amazon guidance; checked October 6, 2026. Not a new program announcement.

findings.title: Estimate the return on your time, not just the bonus percentage
findings.body: A nearly depleted campaign is a weak basis for new production: Amazon’s payment FAQ warns that displayed budgets can lag by up to 48 hours. Build a base-commission-only scenario too. Illustrative math, not a forecast: 10 eligible sales × $30 × a hypothetical 10% bonus = $30 extra; less $12 production cost leaves $18 before other costs and tax. That is $9 per hour if the work takes two hours, excluding any base commissions.
findings.action: Compare three suitable products using low/base/high estimates of eligible sales before the bonus ends. Include acquisition, generation/editing and tool costs plus staff time. Prefer a small pilot using an existing asset when its underlying claims and product fit remain accurate.
findings.measure: Track realized net contribution per production hour. Compare the estimate with shipped/non-returned eligible results after reporting settles; keep base earnings separate from temporary bonuses.
findings.evidence: Amazon payment FAQ supports the budget-lag point; the model, inputs, thresholds and arithmetic are our own planning proposal. No conversion benchmark or income guarantee is implied.
findings.source_date: Amazon FAQ undated, checked October 6, 2026. Example created for this report.

findings.title: Keep sale bonuses and click payments separate
findings.topic: Affiliate+ versus Sponsored Products for Creators
findings.body: Sponsored Products for Creators pays eligible creators for qualifying clicks. Affiliate+ is a sales-bonus model. Amazon’s guides say that when a creator joins both for the same ASIN, Affiliate+ takes priority; do not forecast both campaign payments together. The guides describe a transition to the click campaign after Affiliate+ ends or its budget is depleted, subject to remaining eligibility and budget.
findings.action: Label each reviewed offer by program. Calculate each model separately using its actual displayed terms, and ask a human to confirm overlap handling before making a selection. Do not extrapolate onsite Influencer earnings to offsite Associate links.
findings.measure: Compare verified click-campaign revenue per qualifying click with Affiliate+ bonus revenue per eligible sale. Track base commissions separately and avoid adding the same campaign earnings twice.
findings.evidence: Primary Amazon creator and brand guide excerpts, corroborated by Amazon Ads program description. Full PDF retrieval failed; current account-specific terms must still be checked by the account owner.
findings.source_date: Guides undated, checked October 6, 2026; Amazon Ads Sponsored Products page states updated August 27, 2026.

findings.title: Measure link activity separately from payable traffic
findings.body: URL Vue advertises click, device and operating-system analytics. Amazon’s Sponsored Products for Creators guide defines qualifying clicks and excludes invalid traffic such as bots. These are different measurements: a link-service counter is not proof of payable Amazon traffic or a purchase.
findings.action: For one existing promotion, have a human compare the same date range across available link details, Amazon clicks or qualifying-click reports, and earnings. Label each metric by its source; do not assume the counters should match. No link test was run.
findings.measure: Use the relevant Amazon reported figures for earnings calculations. Keep link-service activity as a separate diagnostic metric, and note reporting lag and any differences in metric definitions.
findings.evidence: Public vendor feature description plus primary Amazon guide excerpt. No claim that URL Vue’s public documentation confirms a particular bot-filtering method; no account analytics were audited.

findings.title: Plan around October 13 maintenance
findings.kind: New official notice; conflicting end times
findings.body: Viral Vue announced maintenance on October 6 at 15:54 UTC. The live status page heading schedules October 13, 09:00–10:00 UTC, while its description says 09:00–11:00 UTC and warns that the Creator Dashboard and extension will be unavailable. In Córdoba those windows are 6–7 a.m. and 6–8 a.m., respectively.
findings.action: Allow for the wider 6–8 a.m. Córdoba window on October 13 and recheck the notice closer to the date. This is planned downtime, not evidence of a current full outage.
findings.measure: Verify the final window and completion on the official status page before relying on the tools during that period.
findings.evidence: Official public status page read live in Chrome; announcement also visible in Viral Vue. The web-search copy was stale and did not contain the notice. End-time discrepancy is unresolved.
findings.source_date: Posted October 6, 2026, 15:54 UTC; maintenance scheduled October 13, 2026.

reports.attention: New planned-maintenance notice for October 13: allow 6–8 a.m. Córdoba time pending clarification of conflicting end times. No immediate account change is needed. The earlier Facebook access limitation was resolved in the later follow-up; the October 3 Creator Studio incident remains listed.
tldr: Review five existing products before committing to more production.
Keep raw link activity separate from Amazon qualifying clicks and earnings.
Allow for Viral Vue maintenance October 13, 6–8 a.m. Córdoba; recheck the conflicting end times.
The approved Facebook session was verified and reviewed later today. No posting, messaging or campaign actions were taken.
reports.next_focus: Creative production: distinguish accurate AI-assisted promotional concepts from product demonstrations and endorsements, checking Amazon, platform and disclosure requirements against primary sources.

reports.title: Make the next five affiliate posts more useful—and measurable
reports.intro: Today’s opportunity is to improve the content and links already in use. These are established practices and proposed tests, not newly announced features or proven earnings gains.
reports.scope: Amazon.com US is the working assumption. This brief covers offsite Associates links; it does not assume participation in onsite Influencer, Creator Connections or SPCC programs.
reports.coverage: Prepared from today’s completed public-source research. No account performance audit or experiment was run. The private group was not rescanned in the broader research pass.

findings.title: Start with five posts that already attract interest
findings.body: Use Amazon tracking IDs and product reports to learn whether the main problem is getting clicks or turning those clicks into orders.
findings.action: Pick five existing posts. Record their product, channel, views where available, Amazon clicks, ordered items and reported commissions before changing one factor.
findings.measure: Compare clicks per content view and commissions per reported click. Allow for reporting and shipment delays.
findings.evidence: Official Amazon capability; suggested prioritization is analyst inference

findings.title: Help someone decide whether the product fits their life
findings.body: Build the next review around a specific use case, an honest demonstration, one advantage and one limitation. Google recommends original evidence and useful comparisons for reviews; a social conversion benefit remains a hypothesis.
findings.action: Test this structure on one suitable product using real product knowledge. AI visuals are creative concepts, not evidence of hands-on experience or product results.
findings.measure: Compare clicks and eventual ordered items with similar content. Keep product and offer comparable.
findings.evidence: Google primary guidance supports original evidence, comparisons, measurements, drawbacks and specific use cases; cross-platform conversion uplift remains a hypothesis

findings.title: Test the mobile buying path before replacing links
findings.body: Native Amazon links and URL Vue can route visitors differently. The available documentation does not establish a universal conversion advantage for either.
findings.action: Have a human review the actual source-app path and tracking ID. If testing routes, keep the product, audience, offer and disclosure comparable.
findings.measure: Review commissions per reported click, clicks per content view and any link-service cost over enough traffic and reporting time.
findings.evidence: Amazon and Viral Vue capability documentation; no independent universal deep-link uplift established

findings.title: Give YouTube Shorts viewers a clickable next step
findings.body: YouTube says URLs in Shorts descriptions and comments are not clickable. A related-video link can lead to a full review; external description links in long-form videos require advanced features.
findings.action: If YouTube is an active channel, connect a relevant Short to its full review and put a clearly disclosed product link in that review’s description.
findings.measure: Measure related-review visits, Amazon clicks per view and later reported commissions. No need to create a new channel for this test.

reports.attention: No newly verified urgent issue was found in this research pass. The previously reported Creator Studio compatibility incident is not a new alert.
tldr: Start with five existing posts and establish a performance baseline before changing anything.
Test one useful change at a time: a clearer buying decision or a better link path.
Treat AI assets as creative concepts; use real evidence for product demonstrations and claims.
No new urgent action was identified in this pass.
reports.next_focus: Campaign selection and economics, checked against current Amazon documentation; tailor recommendations when the main traffic channel is known.
